West Virginia plans to fund state income tax elimination using AI data center revenues, but locals may pay the price in utility bills. 🌐

West Virginia looks to AI data center boom to help eliminate state income tax
Evidence: Tax Cuts, Utility Hikes, Local Autonomy
#USPol #AI

Governor Patrick Morrisey unveiled a plan to dedicate 50% of revenue from hyperscale AI data centers to systematically reduce and eventually eliminate the state personal income tax.
Stated Judgement: (+1.20, +1.00) — Greater Good

While promising tax relief, the plan relies on data centers that create few permanent jobs, strain local power grids, raise utility bills, and bypass local zoning laws under a 2025 state mandate.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.40, -0.30) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: CONDITIONAL — The Path of Revelation. Shifting the tax burden to corporate energy consumers sounds ideal, but it risks trading income tax for higher local utility bills and environmental strain.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 4.5, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Patrick Morrisey: COND (-0.35, -0.25) — Promotes tax cuts while ignoring utility impacts.
- Local Autonomy: FAIL (-0.80, -0.70) — State law strips local zoning control.
West Virginia is leveraging its energy resources to attract massive AI data centers, promising to use the tax revenues to completely phase out the state's personal income tax.

The Poison:
Data centers consume immense amounts of electricity and water. By fast-tracking these projects, the state risks driving up utility costs for residents, offsetting any gains from income tax cuts.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHERE vs WHY error. The state focuses on the abstract financial benefit (WHY we want tax cuts) while ignoring the physical reality of where the massive energy and water demands will be extracted from local communities.

Social Physics Analysis:
This represents a Smart Selfish Loop. The state government uses the popular pretext of tax elimination to justify stripping local communities of their zoning rights, projecting a future of tech prosperity while hiding the immediate infrastructure strain.

The Trajectory: The Path of Revelation.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The physical costs of hosting AI infrastructure will eventually reveal the hidden trade-offs of the tax cut.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI data centers require massive physical resources that strain local grids and water supplies.

The Unavoidable Lie: Eliminating the income tax through data center revenue is a completely free lunch with no hidden costs to residents.

Alethekanon:
Politicians frequently offer highly visible tax cuts to mask the quiet, regressive shifting of infrastructure costs onto local utility payers.

Awwthekanon:
We must protect our beautiful natural resources and ensure that local communities have a voice in the projects built in their own backyards.

Brothekanon:
Bro, getting rid of income tax sounds amazing until your power bill doubles because an AI chatbot farm moved in next door.

Spirithekanon:
"For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first and count the cost, whether he has enough to finish it?" Luke 14:28 PASS
True stewardship requires counting the full physical and social costs before rushing into speculative expansion.

Contractors removed three Confederate statues from Virginia’s Capitol Square on Friday under a line item written into the state budget passed by the General Assembly in June.

Workers took down the statue of Confederate Gen. Thomas “Stonewall” Jackson, which had stood on the grounds since 1875. Crews also took down a statue of Confederate Army surgeon Dr. Hunter Holmes McGuire. It went up in 1904. The third depicted William “Extra Billy” Smith, a Confederate general who twice served as Virginia governor and dated to 1906.
